artifact.canonical_name: Safe URL / agent link data-exfiltration safeguards

claims.text: OpenAI published a January 28 engineering note describing a URL-based data-exfiltration threat in which prompt-injected content can induce an agent to fetch a URL carrying conversation-derived secrets.

The described safeguard allows automatic retrieval for URLs independently observed as public and otherwise blocks the fetch or requires explicit user action; OpenAI presents this as one layer in a defense-in-depth strategy.

limitations: The mechanism targets URL-based exfiltration and does not establish that arbitrary web content is safe or that prompt injection is solved generally.
Security properties are implementation claims from OpenAI and are not independently penetration-tested here.
overrides.why_this_special: Directly captures the security architecture forced by agents that browse and act on external content.
overrides.rationale: Primary-source evidence supports Candidate Selection for a material January 2026 technical change.

artifact.canonical_name: Prompt Injection Attacks on Agentic Coding Assistants

claims.text: The paper is a Systematization of Knowledge on prompt-injection attacks across agentic coding assistants, skills, tools, and protocol ecosystems, and proposes a three-dimensional attack taxonomy.

The abstract reports a synthesis of 78 studies, 42 attack techniques, and 18 defense mechanisms; aggregate attack/defense percentages are author-reported meta-analysis results rather than a new controlled benchmark.

limitations: This is a literature synthesis; its aggregate percentages depend on heterogeneous studies and should not be narrated as a single reproducible experiment.
The retained source is arXiv v1 from January; later research may revise the landscape.
overrides.why_this_special: Provides independent research context for why expanding tool, MCP, file, and shell access changes the security boundary of coding agents.
overrides.rationale: Primary-source evidence supports Candidate Selection for a material January 2026 technical change.

artifact.organization: Xiang Li, Ning Yan, Masood Mortazavi

claims.text: GiG structures embodied-agent memory as graph-connected execution traces, retrieves structurally similar priors, and adds bounded symbolic lookahead for planning.
The abstract reports Pass@1 gains on Robotouille and ALFWorld benchmarks; those figures are author-reported and were not independently reproduced for this survey.

limitations: The task locator is arXiv v3, whose record was updated after January; January chronology is the original submission date while technical wording may reflect later revisions.
Embodied-planning benchmark gains do not directly establish production physical-agent reliability.
overrides.why_this_special: Useful bridge toward physical/embodied agents, but secondary to January’s better-supported software-agent and runtime convergence.
overrides.rationale: Retain as bounded supporting/background evidence; do not allocate a standalone core story at the current page budget.

artifact.canonical_name: DynaWeb: Model-Based Reinforcement Learning of Web Agents

claims.text: DynaWeb trains a web world model to predict page representations from agent actions, then uses it as a synthetic environment for model-based reinforcement learning rollouts.
The paper reports improvements on WebArena and WebVoyager for open-source web-agent models; these are author-reported experimental results.

limitations: A simulated web world model can differ materially from adversarial, dynamic live-web behavior.
The task locator is arXiv v2 updated after January; chronology should use the original January submission.
overrides.why_this_special: Shows a concrete training response to the cost and risk of letting increasingly autonomous web agents learn directly on the live internet.
overrides.rationale: Primary-source evidence supports Candidate Selection for a material January 2026 technical change.

artifact.canonical_name: SYNTHAGENT: synthetic tasks, simulated tools, rubric rewards

claims.text: SYNTHAGENT synthesizes tool-use tasks and mock tool environments, includes an LLM user simulator for missing private information, and constructs task-level rubric rewards.
The paper reports gains across 14 math, search, and tool-use datasets, including small models outperforming larger baselines; these are author-reported results.

limitations: Synthetic environments provide stability but may underrepresent failures and adversarial conditions of real APIs.
The task locator is v2 updated after January; chronology should use the original submission date.
overrides.why_this_special: Complements the month’s product-agent shift with an open training mechanism for smaller tool-using agents.
overrides.rationale: Primary-source evidence supports Candidate Selection for a material January 2026 technical change.
